newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Jan 10.

text.p: RABAT, Jan 10 (Reuter - These are the leading stories in Morocco's weekly economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracey.
- Crackdown on smuggling had positive impact on taxation with a 15 percent increase of receipts from VAT on imports and a 30 percent rise in receipts of local VAT during second half of 1996.

- North African and Continental Insurance Company (CNIA) envisages ceding part of its capital through the stock exchange. The plan to transfer the company to the private sector includes two or three percent of the capital being reserved for employees.

- Morocco's entry into the club of emerging countries through the index of Societe Financiere Internationale (SFI) puts it in direct competition with three others countries in the Middle East and North Africa zone. Anglo-Saxon funds will now be comparing the attractions of Morocco with Egypt, Jordan and Tunisia.

- National Electricity Utility (ONE) says during board meeting there will be no increase in bills in 1997. Industrial buyers of ONE will benefit from a 2.3 percent reduction of tariffs because of the suppression of differential transport cost.

- Some stocks surge, lifting the Casablanca Bourse higher since the end of last year, like Wafabank, ONA group and, in the food sector, companies like breweries Brasseries du Maroc and Branoma and dairy concern Centrale Laitiere.

- After World Bank report on Morocco, drastic measures were expected, to reduce red tape and reform the judiciary and the education. But beyond crackdown on smuggling, which can only improve ethics, little major has been undertaken. These kind of actions cannot replace an economic policy.
- Morocco will have a population of 45 million in the year 2060, with fewer people in the countryside.
- Training centre opened for airtraffic controllers.
